answer: A seismic sensor node checks identity. Each applicant bolts a sensor to a basalt footing, so moving it breaks its location fingerprint, houses it in a cedar enclosure, and times readings with a crystal oscillator. It streams data for 60 days; its seismic noise must match its site, and duplicates within 500m are rejected. Random challenges demand a live reply in seconds. One fake identity costs about $150 plus site and power, and each extra one needs another site and 60 days, so cost scales linearly. Limits: renters suffer and readings can be replayed, so audits and slashing must back it.
